title: awesome-jev catalog entry
description: One public example of Jev (TypeSafe AI's System One decision model) being used. Every entry must be attributable via sources[] and must point at a link that was reachable on the date in checked.

slug.description: Stable kebab-case id, unique within the catalog. Never reuse a slug for a different entry.

title.description: Title as published at the source, not a rewritten one.

summary.description: One-line English description of what this example actually demonstrates, written for a scannable list.

summary_source.description: Where the words of summary come from; the same disclosure for the English text that zh_machine makes for the Chinese. `upstream-description`: the linked repository's own GitHub description, identical apart from letter case, runs of whitespace and one final full stop; scripts/refresh_metadata.py sets it whenever the two match. `upstream-description-stale`: labelled upstream-description once, and no longer identical to the description GitHub serves (the project changed it, or the summary kept only part of it); the words are still the project's. `curated`: a person wrote the summary for this catalogue; only a person sets it, and the refresh never changes it. Absent: not recorded. Anyone who rewrites a summary sets `curated`, or the refresh will call the new text stale.

summary_zh.description: One-line Chinese description. Hand-written unless zh_machine is true.

zh_machine.description: True when summary_zh was machine-translated rather than written by hand. The READMEs report the split rather than claiming every row is hand-written.

url.description: Canonical link for this example. The one link a reader is told to open.

kind.description: The form this example takes. What a reader will find when they open the link.

patterns.description: Which Jev decision patterns this example demonstrates. This is the primary axis of the catalog: the resource form changes, the decision pattern is what stays useful.

question_types.description: Which Jev question primitives the example actually calls. The yes/no primitive is named `noul`, not `binary`. Omit when the entry contains no code.

languages.description: Programming languages the example's code is written in. Omit when there is no code.

platforms.description: How the example reaches Jev: directly, or through a gateway or framework.

name.description: Display name as shown at the source.

handle.description: Platform handle, when it differs from the display name.

repo.description: Source repository, when the entry has one and it differs from url.

stars.description: Repository stars on the date in checked. A popularity signal, not a quality verdict.

repo_license.description: SPDX identifier of the linked project's own licence, or "unknown" when the project ships none. This is the code's licence, not this row's.

package.description: Published package, when the example is installable.

evidence.description: The file this row's code was read in, so a machine can re-check it: the call site, or what evidence.kind says the file shows instead. Required, or evidence_none in its place, when question_types is set, and when has_code is true and url or repo is a GitHub repository (scripts/lint.py enforces both; a retired row's repository is gone and is exempt from the second). scripts/verify_claims.py fetches path from the repo's default branch and asserts every string in matched still appears. Deliberately not pinned to a commit: the point is to notice when a claim stops being true upstream.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the file the call site is in.

matched.description: Strings found in that file that substantiate the claim — an import, an endpoint, a primitive name. Every one must still be present for the row to verify.

kind.description: What the cited file shows. `call-site`: the project calls Jev there. `wire-shape`: the file shows the project speaking Jev's request or response shape rather than building on Jev — a reimplementation, a compatible server, an adapter backed by other models, or a script that sends Jev the same request for comparison; lint requires it on every `kind: alternative` row. `example-only`: the call is in an example or document the project ships, not in its own integration. Absent means `call-site`. A path under an examples/ directory only lists the row in docs/review-queue.md; recording this field is the decision of whoever reads the file.

read_on.description: Date the call site was last read by a person.

evidence_none.description: Why this row carries no machine-checkable evidence — a documentation page, a video, a paywalled article, or code that does not touch Jev. Required instead of evidence when no file can be cited and question_types is set, or has_code is true and url or repo is a GitHub repository. `removed-upstream` means the project removed its Jev integration on purpose; the row stays because why it was removed is the useful part, and notes cite the change. `no-jev-call-site` means the repository's code neither calls Jev nor speaks its request shape — an independent reimplementation with its own interface, or tooling about Jev — so there is no file whose strings would show a relationship to Jev.

official.description: True only when published by TypeSafe AI itself. Community content from the jevai.org site is NOT official.

has_code.description: True when the link contains code a reader could adapt. False for pure prose, news and talking-head video.

published.description: Publication date at the source, when the source states one.

first_seen.description: Date this row entered the catalog.

checked.description: Date url last returned a success status.

link_status.description: HTTP status from the last sweep. Only 2xx belongs in catalog.json; anything else moves to retired.json.

flags.description: Honesty markers a reader deserves before clicking. Kept deliberately blunt.

notes.description: Short English caveat shown next to the row when a reader needs more than the summary.

sources.description: Where this row came from. At least one is required so every row is attributable.

catalog.description: Human name of the upstream index, site or search that surfaced this entry. Two fixed strings name submissions to this repository: 'author submission' when the project's own author or maintainer proposed the row (the row then also carries the self-submitted flag; lint enforces both directions), and 'maintainer submission' when this list's maintainer added it on their own initiative.

license.description: Licence of this row's metadata, not of the linked work. CC-BY-4.0 when descriptive text was inherited from a CC BY 4.0 source (attribution is the sources[] array itself), otherwise CC0-1.0. It does not cover a summary labelled upstream-description or upstream-description-stale in summary_source, nor the row's summary_zh translated from it: those words are the linked project's own.
